title: Mandodari's lament
hookLine: Ravana's queen weeps; Rama gives the enemy his rites
carry: hostility ends at death; even ravana gets his rites
last: SURYA: THE SUN GREETED AS DIVINE LIGHT.

lines: THE WOMEN RUN FROM THE GATES.
cards: When a notorious person dies, the internet celebrates; the jokes arrive within minutes. And somewhere, off-camera, a woman sits on a kitchen floor who has just lost her husband. The war is over.
The monkeys are cheering. Ravana lies on the battlefield. Out through the gates of Lanka come the women of the palace, weeping, running to his body.
At the front is his chief queen, Mandodari. And the Ramayana, a story that spent weeks building Ravana up as the enemy, stops everything to let her speak.

teach.b: Mandodari is the daughter of Maya, the great architect of the demons, and in the tradition she is wise and good. In the tradition, she begged Ravana to send Sita back. He wouldn't listen.
Now she kneels by his body, and Valmiki gives her lament room. She remembers his greatness: the king who conquered the gods, who made the worlds tremble. She can't believe he's lying in the dust.

teach.h: I WARNED YOU. AND I LOVED YOU.
teach.b: She tells him, in effect: I warned you. Your desire for another man's wife is what killed you. And in the same breath, she weeps for him with her whole heart.
She doesn't pretend he was innocent, or that she didn't love him. Both are true at once. Then Rama does something just as striking.
Vibhishana, Ravana's brother, hesitates to perform the funeral rites: why honor a man who did such wrong?
Rama tells him, in Valmiki's telling, that hostility ends at death. The fight is over. He was your brother.
Give him his rites. And Ravana is cremated with the honors of a king.
That's a Hindu teaching, not just a kind moment: the last rites, antyeshti, the final offering, are owed to every person, and Rama puts it plainly: hostility ends at death.
Every villain was somebody's son, somebody's husband. The Ramayana doesn't let you cheer at a funeral.

A traditional Sanskrit verse names five honored women, the panchakanya, and Mandodari is one of them, with Ahalya, Draupadi and Tara. Her grief is honored, not mocked. Compassion for the fallen doesn't excuse anything.
It just refuses to forget that someone loved him.

how: Mandodari is remembered in Hindu tradition as a wise and virtuous queen and is named in a well-known Sanskrit verse listing five revered women, the panchakanya, traditionally recited in the morning.

o: the cheers in Rama's camp at Ravana's fall
a queen grieving the husband she had warned
a curse Mandodari laid on Rama for the war

games.q: who did what — tap the pairs.
p: grieved the king she had warned

s: Mandodari had encouraged Ravana to keep Sita
in the tradition, she begged him to send Sita back.
Ravana was cremated with the honors of a king
at Rama's urging, Vibhishana performed his brother's rites.
Mandodari pretends Ravana did nothing wrong
she says plainly his desire killed him, and grieves him with her whole heart.

games.q: you're Rama. the war is won, and Ravana's brother doesn't want to perform the rites for a man who did such wrong. what do you say?
o: leave the body. he earned it.
perform the rites. hostility ends at death.
let the women of Lanka decide.
games.why: Rama tells Vibhishana that hostility ends at death: he was your brother, give him his rites. Ravana is cremated as a king.

practice: Think of someone who fell, someone in the news or in your family who did real harm and paid for it, and without excusing it, picture the person who loved them, a mother, a husband, a child, and what they're feeling tonight.
Hold both, what was wrong and the grief. If you pray, you can hold those mourners in your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Mandodari's lament. Ravana's queen, kneeling by his body, grieving the king she warned and still loved.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Mandodari, Ravana's chief queen, daughter of Maya the architect.

carryVoice: Your line: hostility ends at death; even Ravana gets his rites. And someone loved him. Gently, till tomorrow.
